2:Matplotlib includes a framework for arbitrary geometric transformations that is used to
3:determine the final position of all elements drawn on the canvas.
4:
5:Transforms are composed into trees of `TransformNode` objects
6:whose actual value depends on their children.  When the contents of
7:children change, their parents are automatically invalidated.  The
8:next time an invalidated transform is accessed, it is recomputed to
9:reflect those changes.  This invalidation/caching approach prevents
10:unnecessary recomputations of transforms, and contributes to better
11:interactive performance.
12:
13:For example, here is a graph of the transform tree used to plot data to the figure:
14:
15:.. graphviz:: /api/transforms.dot
16:    :alt: Diagram of transform tree from data to figure coordinates.
17:
18:The framework can be used for both affine and non-affine
19:transformations.  However, for speed, we want to use the backend
20:renderers to perform affine transformations whenever possible.
21:Therefore, it is possible to perform just the affine or non-affine
22:part of a transformation on a set of data.  The affine is always
23:assumed to occur after the non-affine.  For any transform::
24:
25:  full transform == non-affine part + affine part
26:
27:The backends are not expected to handle non-affine transformations
28:themselves.
29:
30:See the tutorial :ref:`transforms_tutorial` for examples
31:of how to use transforms.
32:"""
33:
34:# Note: There are a number of places in the code where we use `np.min` or
35:# `np.minimum` instead of the builtin `min`, and likewise for `max`.  This is
36:# done so that `nan`s are propagated, instead of being silently dropped.

56:def _make_str_method(*args, **kwargs):
57:    """
58:    Generate a ``__str__`` method for a `.Transform` subclass.
59:
60:    After ::
61:
62:        class T:
63:            __str__ = _make_str_method("attr", key="other")
64:
65:    ``str(T(...))`` will be
66:
67:    .. code-block:: text
68:
69:        {type(T).__name__}(
70:            {self.attr},
71:            key={self.other})
72:    """
73:    indent = functools.partial(textwrap.indent, prefix=" " * 4)
74:    def strrepr(x): return repr(x) if isinstance(x, str) else str(x)
75:    return lambda self: (
76:        type(self).__name__ + "("
77:        + ",".join([*(indent("\n" + strrepr(getattr(self, arg)))
78:                      for arg in args),
79:                    *(indent("\n" + k + "=" + strrepr(getattr(self, arg)))
80:                      for k, arg in kwargs.items())])
81:        + ")")

84:class TransformNode:
85:    """
86:    The base class for anything that participates in the transform tree
87:    and needs to invalidate its parents or be invalidated.  This includes
88:    classes that are not really transforms, such as bounding boxes, since some
89:    transforms depend on bounding boxes to compute their values.
90:    """
91:
92:    # Invalidation may affect only the affine part.  If the
93:    # invalidation was "affine-only", the _invalid member is set to
94:    # INVALID_AFFINE_ONLY
95:
96:    # Possible values for the _invalid attribute.
97:    _VALID, _INVALID_AFFINE_ONLY, _INVALID_FULL = range(3)
98:
99:    # Some metadata about the transform, used to determine whether an
100:    # invalidation is affine-only
101:    is_affine = False
102:    is_bbox = _api.deprecated("3.9")(_api.classproperty(lambda cls: False))
103:
104:    pass_through = False
105:    """
106:    If pass_through is True, all ancestors will always be
107:    invalidated, even if 'self' is already invalid.
108:    """
109:
110:    def __init__(self, shorthand_name=None):
111:        """
112:        Parameters
113:        ----------
114:        shorthand_name : str
115:            A string representing the "name" of the transform. The name carries
116:            no significance other than to improve the readability of
117:            ``str(transform)`` when DEBUG=True.
118:        """
119:        self._parents = {}
120:        # Initially invalid, until first computation.
121:        self._invalid = self._INVALID_FULL
122:        self._shorthand_name = shorthand_name or ''
123:
124:    if DEBUG:
125:        def __str__(self):
126:            # either just return the name of this TransformNode, or its repr
127:            return self._shorthand_name or repr(self)
128:
129:    def __getstate__(self):
130:        # turn the dictionary with weak values into a normal dictionary
131:        return {**self.__dict__,
132:                '_parents': {k: v() for k, v in self._parents.items()}}
133:
134:    def __setstate__(self, data_dict):
135:        self.__dict__ = data_dict
136:        # turn the normal dictionary back into a dictionary with weak values
137:        # The extra lambda is to provide a callback to remove dead
138:        # weakrefs from the dictionary when garbage collection is done.
139:        self._parents = {
140:            k: weakref.ref(v, lambda _, pop=self._parents.pop, k=k: pop(k))
141:            for k, v in self._parents.items() if v is not None}
142:
143:    def __copy__(self):
144:        other = copy.copy(super())
145:        # If `c = a + b; a1 = copy(a)`, then modifications to `a1` do not
146:        # propagate back to `c`, i.e. we need to clear the parents of `a1`.
147:        other._parents = {}
148:        # If `c = a + b; c1 = copy(c)`, then modifications to `a` also need to
149:        # be propagated to `c1`.
150:        for key, val in vars(self).items():
151:            if isinstance(val, TransformNode) and id(self) in val._parents:
152:                other.set_children(val)  # val == getattr(other, key)
153:        return other
154:
155:    def invalidate(self):
156:        """
157:        Invalidate this `TransformNode` and triggers an invalidation of its
158:        ancestors.  Should be called any time the transform changes.
159:        """
160:        return self._invalidate_internal(
161:            level=self._INVALID_AFFINE_ONLY if self.is_affine else self._INVALID_FULL,
162:            invalidating_node=self)
163:
164:    def _invalidate_internal(self, level, invalidating_node):
165:        """
166:        Called by :meth:`invalidate` and subsequently ascends the transform
167:        stack calling each TransformNode's _invalidate_internal method.
168:        """
169:        # If we are already more invalid than the currently propagated invalidation,
170:        # then we don't need to do anything.
171:        if level <= self._invalid and not self.pass_through:
172:            return
173:        self._invalid = level
174:        for parent in list(self._parents.values()):
175:            parent = parent()  # Dereference the weak reference.
176:            if parent is not None:
177:                parent._invalidate_internal(level=level, invalidating_node=self)
178:
179:    def set_children(self, *children):
180:        """
181:        Set the children of the transform, to let the invalidation
182:        system know which transforms can invalidate this transform.
183:        Should be called from the constructor of any transforms that
184:        depend on other transforms.
185:        """
186:        # Parents are stored as weak references, so that if the
187:        # parents are destroyed, references from the children won't
188:        # keep them alive.
189:        id_self = id(self)
190:        for child in children:
191:            # Use weak references so this dictionary won't keep obsolete nodes
192:            # alive; the callback deletes the dictionary entry. This is a
193:            # performance improvement over using WeakValueDictionary.
194:            ref = weakref.ref(
195:                self, lambda _, pop=child._parents.pop, k=id_self: pop(k))
196:            child._parents[id_self] = ref
197:
198:    def frozen(self):
199:        """
200:        Return a frozen copy of this transform node.  The frozen copy will not
201:        be updated when its children change.  Useful for storing a previously
202:        known state of a transform where ``copy.deepcopy()`` might normally be
203:        used.
204:        """
205:        return self

210:    The base class of all bounding boxes.
211:
212:    This class is immutable; `Bbox` is a mutable subclass.
213:
214:    The canonical representation is as two points, with no
215:    restrictions on their ordering.  Convenience properties are
216:    provided to get the left, bottom, right and top edges and width
217:    and height, but these are not stored explicitly.
218:    """
219:

221:    is_affine = True

224:        @staticmethod
225:        def _check(points):
226:            if isinstance(points, np.ma.MaskedArray):
227:                _api.warn_external("Bbox bounds are a masked array.")
228:            points = np.asarray(points)
229:            if any((points[1, :] - points[0, :]) == 0):
230:                _api.warn_external("Singular Bbox.")
231:
232:    def frozen(self):
233:        return Bbox(self.get_points().copy())
234:    frozen.__doc__ = TransformNode.__doc__
235:
236:    def __array__(self, *args, **kwargs):
237:        return self.get_points()
238:

240:    def x0(self):
241:        """
242:        The first of the pair of *x* coordinates that define the bounding box.
243:
244:        This is not guaranteed to be less than :attr:`x1` (for that, use
245:        :attr:`xmin`).
246:        """

253:
